site.name: Atlas Mine & Mill Complex
site.componentDetail: Atlas Mine workings and the associated Atlas stamp-mill ruins near Sneffels form one historic mining-and-processing complex; keep the neighboring Revenue–Virginius property separate.
overview: The Atlas Mine and its stamp mill were part of the Sneffels mining district above Canyon Creek in Ouray County. The operation was established during the first major wave of mining development in the district in 1876 and produced precious-metal ore that was processed at the associated mill.

Federal geologic reporting documented active work at the Atlas in 1913 and examined the Klondike vein at depths ranging from roughly 850 to 1,500 feet. The surviving mill site and tailings remain the most visible historic features of the complex.

timeline.text: The Atlas operation was established during the early development of the Sneffels mining district.
U.S. Geological Survey field work documented active mining on the Klondike vein at the Atlas Mine at depths of about 850 to 1,500 feet.
The Atlas stamp mill was an important early producer in the Sneffels district and processed ore from the mine complex.
Abandoned-mine reclamation work has addressed portions of the Atlas mill and tailings area, so present-day landforms should not be assumed to match the operating-era site exactly.

moreHistory: The Atlas was one of a number of mines developed around Sneffels in the upper Canyon Creek drainage. Its mine workings and processing mill should be interpreted together as a linked industrial complex rather than as unrelated locations.
Remnant uses the historic Atlas mine locality as the identification anchor for the complex. The coordinate is a site-level historic reference, not a field survey of a safe or accessible mine opening.
Do not enter mine workings or climb on mill ruins, machinery remnants, tailings, or unstable slopes. Historic mining features in the area may be altered by weather, avalanches, and reclamation.
